page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.6xlarge is a dedicated high-clock-speed instance powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8269CY processor clocked at a baseline of 3.1 GHz. The instance provisions 24 vCPUs across 12 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, backed by 35 MB of L3 cache, 1 MB L2 cache per core, and support for AVX-512 vector extensions including AVX-512 VNNI. The system is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB per vCPU.

Network connectivity features an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth under the KVM hypervisor. The instance includes no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached block storage volumes for persistent data and operating system installations. There are no discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs provisioned on this configuration, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

Benchmark testing situates the instance consistently within the middle 50 percent tier across all evaluated metrics. Compute workloads demonstrate a multi-core stress-ng score of 23,015.19 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9,875.0, with single-core performance scoring 1,438.39 in stress-ng and 1,287.0 in Geekbench. In memory testing, large-block uncached read and write bandwidths reached 109.43 GB/sec and 48.03 GB/sec, respectively. Application-level metrics recorded 22.14 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, software compilation throughput of 19,039.0 points in Geekbench Clang testing, and static web serving throughput of 17.13 GB/sec.

Given its combination of a 3.1 GHz base CPU frequency, 24 dedicated virtual cores, and 96 GB of memory, ecs.hfg6.6xlarge is structured for compute-heavy enterprise applications, build pipelines, CI/CD compilation, in-memory caching systems, and medium-scale web and application serving where steady-state CPU performance without storage bundling is desired.
